questions.text: What is the name for a survey that collects data from every member of a population?

options: A census
A sample
A pilot study
A hypothesis
feedback: A sample uses only part of the population
A pilot study is a small trial run before the main survey
A hypothesis is a statement that can be tested

questions.solution: A census collects data from every member of the population, while a sample uses only part of it
questions.hint: Think about the survey the government carries out of every household

questions.text: What is the name for a list of all the members of a population, from which a sample can be chosen? Give the term.
questions.solution: A sampling frame is a list of every member of the population, such as a school register
questions.hint: Think of a school register or an electoral roll that you pick names from

questions.text: Which of these is qualitative data?

options: The colours of cars in a car park
The heights of students
The number of goals in a match
The masses of apples
feedback: Heights are numbers, so they are quantitative
Numbers of goals are quantitative
Masses are numbers, so they are quantitative

questions.solution: Qualitative data is described in words, not numbers, like colours
questions.hint: Qualitative data is not numerical

questions.text: Which of these is continuous data?

options: The time taken to run 100 m
The number of pets a student owns
The number of cars in a car park
The number of pages in a book
feedback: Numbers of pets can only be whole numbers, so this is discrete
Numbers of cars are counted, so this is discrete
Numbers of pages are counted, so this is discrete

questions.solution: Continuous data is measured and can take any value in a range, like a time
questions.hint: Continuous data is measured rather than counted

questions.text: Data that you collect yourself, for your own investigation, is called what type of data? Give one word.

feedback.secondary: Secondary data has already been collected by someone else
feedback.secondary data: Secondary data has already been collected by someone else

questions.solution: Primary data is collected by you, for your own purpose
questions.hint: It is the first-hand kind of data, not data collected by someone else

questions.text: What is a pilot study?

options: A small trial run to test a survey or experiment before the main study
A survey of every member of the population
A list of all the members of a population
A statement that can be tested

questions.solution: A pilot study is a small trial run that finds problems with a survey or experiment before the main study
questions.hint: It happens before the main survey, on a small group

questions.text: Which type of data can only take particular values, such as the number of people in a car?

options: Discrete data
Continuous data
Qualitative data
feedback: Continuous data can take any value in a range, such as a length
The number of people is a number, so it is quantitative, not qualitative

questions.solution: Discrete data can only take particular values, usually whole numbers that are counted
questions.hint: Can there be 2.7 people in a car?

questions.text: Data that has already been collected by someone else, such as figures from a government website, is called what type of data? Give one word.

feedback.primary: Primary data is collected by you, for your own investigation
feedback.primary data: Primary data is collected by you, for your own investigation

questions.solution: Secondary data has been collected by someone else, for example published statistics
questions.hint: It is second-hand data

questions.text: What is the difference between a census and a sample?

options: A census uses every member of the population; a sample uses only part of it
A census uses only part of the population; a sample uses every member
A census is always biased; a sample never is
A census uses secondary data; a sample uses primary data

questions.solution: A census collects data from the whole population; a sample collects data from part of it
questions.hint: Think about how much of the population each one includes

questions.text: Data that is not numerical, such as favourite colours, is called what type of data? Give one word.
questions.solution: Data described in words, such as colours, is qualitative (categorical) data
questions.hint: It is the opposite of quantitative

questions.text: In an experiment, which variable is deliberately changed by the person carrying out the experiment? Give the term.

feedback.response variable: The response variable is the one that is measured
feedback.response: The response variable is the one that is measured
feedback.dependent variable: The dependent (response) variable is the one that is measured
feedback.dependent: The dependent (response) variable is the one that is measured

questions.solution: The explanatory (independent) variable is the one the experimenter changes; the response variable is measured
questions.hint: It is the variable that explains changes in the results

questions.text: In an experiment, the variable that is measured to see whether it is affected, such as the height of a plant, is called the ... variable. Give the missing word.

feedback.explanatory: The explanatory variable is the one that is changed
feedback.explanatory variable: The explanatory variable is the one that is changed
feedback.independent: The independent (explanatory) variable is the one that is changed
feedback.independent variable: The independent (explanatory) variable is the one that is changed

questions.solution: The response (dependent) variable is measured; it may respond to changes in the explanatory variable
questions.hint: It is the variable that responds to the change

questions.text: A questionnaire is first tried out on a small group of people to find any problems before the main survey. Give the name for this trial.
questions.solution: This is a pilot study: a small trial that finds problems before the main survey
questions.hint: The word is also used for the person who flies a plane

questions.text: Which of these is a reason for taking a sample rather than a census?

options: A sample is quicker and cheaper to carry out
A sample always gives more accurate results than a census
A sample includes every member of the population
A census can never be carried out

questions.solution: A sample is quicker and cheaper than a census, although it may not represent the population perfectly
questions.hint: Think about the time and cost of asking everyone

questions.text: Which of these is an open question?

options: What do you think about the school canteen?
Do you eat school lunches? (Yes / No)
How many times a week do you eat school lunch? (0, 1–2, 3–4, 5)
Rate the canteen from 1 to 5

questions.solution: An open question lets people answer in any way they like; the others give a fixed set of answers
questions.hint: Which question has no answer boxes to choose from?

questions.text: Jo wants to survey 50 of the 1000 students at her school. She numbers the students from 1 to 1000 and uses a random number generator to pick 50 different numbers. Which sampling method is this?

options: Simple random sampling
Systematic sampling
Quota sampling
Convenience sampling
feedback: Systematic sampling picks every kth name from a list
In quota sampling the interviewer chooses people to fill groups
Convenience sampling uses people who are easy to reach

questions.solution: Every student has the same chance of being chosen by random numbers, so this is simple random sampling
questions.hint: Each student is equally likely to be picked

questions.text: A researcher picks a random starting point from 1 to 20 on a list of names, then chooses every 20th name after it. Name this sampling method.
questions.solution: Choosing every kth item from a list after a random start is systematic sampling
questions.hint: The names are picked at regular intervals

questions.text: An interviewer in a town centre is told to interview 20 men and 20 women. She chooses who to stop. Which sampling method is this?

options: Quota sampling
Stratified sampling
Systematic sampling
Cluster sampling
feedback: In stratified sampling the people in each group are chosen at random, not by the interviewer
Systematic sampling picks every kth item from a list
Cluster sampling chooses whole groups, such as streets or schools

questions.solution: The interviewer fills a fixed number for each group and chooses the people herself, so this is quota sampling
questions.hint: She has a set number of people to find in each group

questions.text: Ali asks the first 30 people who walk past him in a shopping centre. Name this sampling method.
questions.solution: Asking whoever is easiest to reach is convenience (opportunity) sampling
questions.hint: He uses the people who are easiest to reach

questions.text: Which of these is discrete data?

options: The number of text messages sent in a day
The length of a leaf
The time spent on homework
The mass of a bag of flour
feedback: Length is measured, so it is continuous
Time is measured, so it is continuous
Mass is measured, so it is continuous

questions.solution: The number of text messages is counted and can only be a whole number, so it is discrete
questions.hint: Discrete data is counted

questions.text: A sampling frame lists 600 students. Leah wants a systematic sample of 30 students: she chooses one of the first k names at random and then every kth name after it. Work out k.
questions.hint: Divide the size of the population by the size of the sample

questions.text: A survey question has these response boxes: 0–1 hours, 1–2 hours, 2–3 hours, 3 or more hours. What is wrong with them?

options: The boxes overlap, so 1 hour fits in two boxes
There is no box for more than 3 hours
The boxes are not in order
The question should be open

questions.solution: The boxes overlap: 1 hour and 2 hours each fit in two boxes, so the responses are unclear
questions.hint: Which box would someone tick if they spent exactly 1 hour?

questions.text: A survey about exercise is carried out by asking people leaving a gym. Why is this sample likely to be biased?

options: People leaving a gym probably exercise more than most people
The sample is too large
The data collected is secondary
Every person in the town has an equal chance of being chosen

questions.solution: People at a gym are not typical of the whole population, so they are likely to overestimate how much people exercise
questions.hint: Are the people at a gym typical of everyone in the town?

questions.text: Which question is a leading question?

options: Don't you agree that school should start later?
What time do you think school should start?
Should school start later? (Yes / No / Not sure)
How long is your journey to school, in minutes?

questions.solution: A leading question pushes people towards a particular answer, like 'Don't you agree…?'
questions.hint: Which question encourages one particular answer?

questions.text: A sample of 40 is chosen from 400 Year 10 students and 600 Year 11 students. Each year group is represented in proportion to its size, and the students within each year group are chosen at random. Name this sampling method.

feedback.quota: In quota sampling the interviewer chooses the people; here they are chosen at random
feedback.quota sampling: In quota sampling the interviewer chooses the people; here they are chosen at random

questions.solution: Splitting the population into groups and taking a proportional random sample from each is stratified sampling
questions.hint: The population is split into groups (strata) first

questions.text: Sam tests whether a new fertiliser makes tomato plants grow taller. He gives fertiliser to 20 plants and no fertiliser to another 20 plants. What is the purpose of the 20 plants with no fertiliser?

options: They are a control group to compare against
They are a pilot study
They make the sample biased
They are the explanatory variable

questions.solution: The plants without fertiliser are a control group, so Sam can compare them with the plants that had fertiliser
questions.hint: What would Sam compare the fertilised plants with?

questions.text: These heights of five students were recorded in cm: 152, 160, 1.58, 149, 165. Which value should be checked when the data is cleaned?
questions.solution: 1.58 looks like a height in metres, not centimetres, so it should be checked (it is probably 158 cm)
questions.hint: Look for a value that does not fit with the units of the others

questions.text: A teacher wants to find the mean time that students at her school spend on homework. She asks 10 students in her own class. Which change would make her estimate more likely to represent the whole school?

options: Use a larger sample chosen at random from the whole school
Ask only the students who finish their homework fastest
Ask the same 10 students again
Use a smaller sample

questions.solution: A larger random sample from the whole school is more likely to represent all the students
questions.hint: Think about sample size and whether the sample represents the whole school

questions.text: A council wants to know what residents think about a new park. It puts a questionnaire on its website and 300 people reply. Which statement is accurate?

options: The sample may be biased because only people who use the website and choose to reply are included
The sample cannot be biased because 300 is a large number
This is a census because everyone could reply
The data is secondary because it was collected online

questions.solution: People choose themselves, and only website users can reply, so the sample may not represent all residents
questions.hint: Who is likely to reply, and who is left out?

questions.text: A student wants to test the hypothesis 'Year 11 students sleep less than Year 7 students'. Which plan would give a fair test?

options: Take a random sample from each year group and compare their mean hours of sleep
Ask five of her Year 11 friends how much they sleep
Ask Year 7 students only
Find the total hours of sleep for the whole school

questions.solution: A random sample from each year group lets her compare the two groups fairly
questions.hint: She needs data from both year groups, chosen without bias

questions.text: Which of these is an advantage of a laboratory experiment compared with a field experiment?

options: Extraneous variables can be controlled more easily
The setting is more like real life
It does not need an explanatory variable
It always uses a larger sample
feedback: Being more like real life is an advantage of a field experiment
Every experiment has an explanatory variable
The sample size does not depend on where the experiment happens

questions.solution: In a laboratory the conditions can be controlled, so other (extraneous) variables are less likely to affect the results
questions.hint: Think about how much control the researcher has in a laboratory

questions.text: Mia wants to estimate how many hours a week students at her school spend playing video games. Which is a correct reason why she should NOT use only her friends as her sample?

options: Her friends may have similar habits, so they may not represent the whole school
Her friends would give secondary data
A sample of her friends would be a census
Friends cannot be asked questions

questions.solution: Friends are likely to be similar to each other, so the sample would be biased
questions.hint: Would her friends be typical of every student in the school?

questions.text: A random sample of 100 people from a town is taken, and 62 of them say they support a new bus route. Which statement is accurate?

options: About 62% of the town might support the route, but another sample could give a different result
Exactly 62% of everyone in the town supports the route
The sample is useless because it does not include everyone
Exactly 62 people in the whole town support the route

questions.solution: A sample gives an estimate for the population, and different samples can give different results
questions.hint: A sample gives an estimate, not an exact answer for the whole town

questions.text: On a scatter diagram, the points go up from left to right. What type of correlation is shown?

options: Positive correlation
Negative correlation
No correlation
feedback: Negative correlation goes down from left to right
With no correlation the points show no pattern

questions.solution: When one variable increases as the other increases, the correlation is positive
questions.hint: Think about what happens to y as x gets bigger

questions.text: What is the name of the straight line drawn through the middle of the points on a scatter diagram to show the trend? Give the term.
questions.solution: A line of best fit is drawn through the middle of the points to show the trend
questions.hint: It is the line that fits the points as well as possible

questions.text: Which five values are shown on a box plot?

options: Minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, maximum
Mean, median, mode, range, total
Minimum, mean, median, mode, maximum
Lower quartile, mean, upper quartile, range, total

questions.solution: A box plot shows the minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum
questions.hint: The box goes from one quartile to the other

questions.text: When the class widths are unequal, what is plotted on the vertical axis of a histogram? Give the term.

feedback.frequency: With unequal class widths, frequency is shown by the area of each bar, not its height
feedback.cumulative frequency: Cumulative frequency is plotted on a cumulative frequency graph, not a histogram

questions.solution: The vertical axis shows frequency density = frequency ÷ class width, so the area of each bar shows the frequency
questions.hint: It is frequency divided by class width

questions.text: What type of graph shows how a value changes over time, such as a shop's monthly sales? Give the name.
questions.solution: A time series graph plots values against time to show how they change
questions.hint: The data is a series of values taken over time

questions.text: In a pie chart, what does the whole circle represent?

options: The total of all the data
The largest category
The mean of the data
The range of the data

questions.solution: The whole circle (360°) represents the total frequency; each sector is a fraction of it
questions.hint: Each sector is a fraction of the whole

questions.text: What is the difference between interpolation and extrapolation?

options: Interpolation estimates inside the range of the data; extrapolation estimates outside it
Interpolation estimates outside the range of the data; extrapolation estimates inside it
Interpolation uses a bar chart; extrapolation uses a pie chart
They mean exactly the same thing

questions.solution: Interpolation estimates within the range of the data; extrapolation goes beyond it and is less reliable
questions.hint: 'Inter' means between and 'extra' means outside

questions.text: Using a line of best fit to estimate a value outside the range of the data is called what? Give the term.

feedback.interpolation: Interpolation estimates inside the range of the data
feedback.interpolating: Interpolation estimates inside the range of the data

questions.solution: Estimating outside the range of the data is extrapolation, which is less reliable than interpolation
questions.hint: 'Extra' means outside

questions.text: The points on a scatter diagram lie very close to a straight line that goes down from left to right. How is the correlation described?

options: Strong negative correlation
Weak negative correlation
Strong positive correlation
No correlation

questions.solution: Going down means negative, and points close to a line means strong: strong negative correlation
questions.hint: Decide the direction first, then how close the points are to a line

questions.text: Complete the saying: 'Correlation does not imply …'. Give the missing word.
questions.solution: Correlation does not imply causation: two variables can be linked without one causing the other
questions.hint: It is about whether one variable makes the other change

questions.text: On a box plot, the length of the box shows which measure of spread? Give the term.

feedback.range: The range is shown by the whiskers from the minimum to the maximum, not just the box

questions.solution: The box runs from the lower quartile to the upper quartile, so its length is the interquartile range
questions.hint: The box goes from one quartile to the other

questions.text: On a cumulative frequency graph for 80 values, which cumulative frequency do you read across from to estimate the median?

feedback: 20 is a quarter of 80: that gives the lower quartile
60 is three quarters of 80: that gives the upper quartile
80 is the total: read from half of it

questions.solution: The median is halfway through the data: 80 ÷ 2 = 40
questions.hint: The median is halfway through the data

questions.text: What is the key of a stem and leaf diagram for?

options: It shows how to read the values, for example 3 | 4 means 34
It shows the mean of the data
It lists the outliers
It gives the frequency density

questions.solution: The key tells you how to read each stem and leaf, for example 3 | 4 means 34 (or 3.4)
questions.hint: Without it, would you know whether 3 | 4 means 34 or 3.4?

questions.text: A class has a width of 10 and a frequency of 35. Work out the frequency density.
questions.solution: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width = 35 ÷ 10 = 3.5
questions.hint: Frequency density = frequency ÷ class width

questions.text: On a scatter diagram of hours of revision against test mark, one student revised for 20 hours but scored much lower than everyone else, who all follow a clear positive trend. What is a point like this called? Give the word.
questions.solution: A point that does not fit the pattern of the rest of the data is an outlier
questions.hint: It lies outside the general pattern

questions.text: In a survey of 120 people, 30 chose blue as their favourite colour. In a pie chart of the results, what angle should the blue sector have? Give your answer in degrees.
questions.hint: Work out the fraction of the people who chose blue, then multiply by 360°

questions.text: A line of best fit should pass through the point whose coordinates are the … of the x values and the … of the y values. Give the missing word (the same word fills both gaps).

feedback.median: The line of best fit passes through the mean point, not the median
feedback.mode: The line of best fit passes through the mean point, not the mode

questions.solution: A line of best fit should pass through the mean point (mean of x, mean of y)
questions.hint: Add up the values and divide by how many there are

questions.text:
Here is a stem and leaf diagram. Key: 2 | 5 means 25.
1 | 3 7 8
2 | 0 4 4 9
3 | 1 6
What is the mode?
questions.solution: The leaf 4 appears twice in the row with stem 2, so 24 is the most common value
questions.hint: Look for a leaf that appears more than once in the same row

questions.text: A histogram has a bar for the class 10 < t ≤ 30 with a frequency density of 2. What is the frequency of this class?

feedback: The class width is 30 - 10 = 20: multiply it by the frequency density
Frequency = frequency density × class width, not class width ÷ frequency density
The class width is 20, not 30

questions.solution: Frequency = frequency density × class width = 2 × 20 = 40
questions.hint: Frequency = frequency density × class width

questions.text: Which pair of variables would you expect to show negative correlation?

options: The age of a car and its value
Height and arm span
Hours of revision and test mark
Temperature and ice cream sales

questions.solution: As a car gets older its value usually falls, which is negative correlation; the others usually increase together
questions.hint: For negative correlation, one variable goes up as the other goes down

questions.text: A box plot for Group X has median 45 and interquartile range 10. A box plot for Group Y has median 52 and interquartile range 25. Which statement is correct?

options: Group Y has the higher median, and Group X is more consistent
Group X has the higher median, and Group Y is more consistent
Group Y has the higher median, and Group Y is more consistent
The two groups have the same spread

questions.solution: Group Y's median (52) is higher; Group X's interquartile range (10) is smaller, so Group X's data is more consistent
questions.hint: Compare the medians, then compare the interquartile ranges: a smaller spread means more consistent

questions.text: A line of best fit has equation y = 2x + 10. It was drawn using data with x values from 5 to 20. Which estimate is the most reliable?

options: The value of y when x = 12
The value of y when x = 40
The value of y when x = 0
The value of y when x = 100

questions.solution: x = 12 is inside the range of the data (interpolation), so it is the most reliable; the others are extrapolation
questions.hint: Which x value lies inside the range of the data?

questions.text: The cumulative frequency for heights up to 160 cm is 18, and up to 170 cm it is 45. How many people are taller than 160 cm but no taller than 170 cm?

feedback: 45 is everyone up to 170 cm: subtract the 18 up to 160 cm
Subtract the cumulative frequencies, don't add them
18 people are up to 160 cm

questions.solution: 45 - 18 = 27 people are in this class
questions.hint: Cumulative frequency is a running total: subtract to find one class

questions.text: A scatter diagram shows that as the number of hours of sunshine increases, the number of umbrellas sold decreases. What type of correlation is this? Give one word.

feedback.positive: One variable goes up while the other goes down
feedback.positive correlation: One variable goes up while the other goes down

questions.solution: As one variable increases the other decreases, so the correlation is negative
questions.hint: One goes up while the other goes down

questions.text: In a histogram, the class 0 < m ≤ 5 has frequency density 4, and the class 5 < m ≤ 15 has frequency density 3. Which class has the greater frequency?

options: 5 < m ≤ 15, with frequency 30
0 < m ≤ 5, with frequency 20
Both classes have frequency 20
0 < m ≤ 5, because its bar is taller

questions.solution: Frequency = frequency density × width: 4 × 5 = 20 and 3 × 10 = 30, so 5 < m ≤ 15 has more
questions.hint: In a histogram the area of a bar shows the frequency

questions.text:
This stem and leaf diagram shows 11 test marks. Key: 4 | 2 means 42.
4 | 2 5 8
5 | 0 3 3 7
6 | 1 4 9
7 | 2
What is the median mark?
questions.solution: There are 11 marks, so the median is the 6th: 42, 45, 48, 50, 53, 53, … The 6th mark is 53
questions.hint: The median of 11 values is the 6th value in order

questions.text: A pie chart shows the favourite sports of 60 students. The football sector has an angle of 132°. How many students chose football?

feedback: 132 is the angle, not the number of students
Each student is 360 ÷ 60 = 6°: divide the angle by 6
Each student is 6°: 132 ÷ 6

questions.solution: Each student is 360° ÷ 60 = 6°, so 132 ÷ 6 = 22 students
questions.hint: Work out how many degrees represent one student

questions.text: A study finds strong positive correlation between ice cream sales and the number of people swimming in the sea. Which statement is accurate?

options: Both may be caused by a third variable, such as hot weather
Buying ice cream makes people go swimming
Swimming makes people buy ice cream
There is no relationship between the two variables

questions.solution: Correlation does not prove causation: hot weather could increase both ice cream sales and swimming
questions.hint: Correlation does not mean one variable causes the other

questions.text: Why is a line of best fit not reliable for predicting a value far outside the range of the data?

options: The trend may not continue outside the range of the data
Lines of best fit only work for negative correlation
A line of best fit always passes through the origin
Values outside the range are always exactly on the line

questions.solution: Extrapolation assumes the trend carries on, which may not be true outside the data
questions.hint: You have no data out there to show what happens

questions.text: A box plot of reaction times has median 0.35 s, lower quartile 0.30 s and upper quartile 0.50 s. What does this suggest about the shape of the distribution?

options: It has positive skew
It has negative skew
It is symmetrical
It has no median
feedback: For negative skew the median would be closer to the upper quartile
For a symmetrical distribution the median would be halfway between the quartiles

questions.solution: Upper quartile - median = 0.15 s is more than median - lower quartile = 0.05 s, so the data has positive skew
questions.hint: Compare the distance from the median to each quartile

questions.text: Which diagram is most suitable for comparing the medians and interquartile ranges of two large sets of continuous data?

options: Two box plots drawn on the same scale
Two pie charts
One bar chart of the two totals
A pictogram

questions.solution: Box plots show the median and quartiles, so two box plots on the same scale make the comparison easy
questions.hint: Which diagram shows the median and the quartiles?

questions.text: A correlation coefficient is -0.95. Describe the correlation in two words (strength and type).

feedback.weak negative: -0.95 is very close to -1, so the correlation is strong
feedback.strong positive: The minus sign means the correlation is negative
feedback.weak positive: The minus sign means negative, and -0.95 is close to -1, so it is strong

questions.solution: -0.95 is close to -1, so this is strong negative correlation
questions.hint: The sign gives the type, and how close it is to 1 or -1 gives the strength

questions.text: Two schools' test marks are shown on box plots. School P: median 58, range 40, interquartile range 12. School Q: median 58, range 35, interquartile range 24. Which statement is accurate?

options: The middle half of School P's marks is more consistent than School Q's
The middle half of School Q's marks is more consistent than School P's
School P has a higher median than School Q
The two schools have identical distributions

questions.solution: The medians are equal; P's interquartile range (12) is smaller than Q's (24), so P's middle 50% of marks is more consistent
questions.hint: The interquartile range is not affected by extreme values, so compare the interquartile ranges
